newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares snap winning streak, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares snap winning streak, end lower.

text.p: Capping a week-long rally, Chilean blue chip shares closed a shade lower in volatile trade although demand remained strong among foreign investors, traders said.
The market is expected to open higher, driven by foreign buy orders, said Henry Rudnick, head of research at CB Capitales.
"Foreign demand has been heavy since Merrill Lynch boosted its Chile weighting last week," said Rudnick.
Merrill Lynch raised Chile's weighting in its portfolio to 14 percent from nine percent, he said.
The weighted IPSA index closed down 0.17 percent at 102.9 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.07 percent to 5,600.8 points.
Turnover remained light at 13 billion pesos.

Although volume is higher than in previous weeks, the fact it has failed to pick up more sharply is a cause for concern as it shows institutional investors are not re-entering the market with any force, said traders.
"Institutional investors are reticent to enter the bolsa," said one dealer. "They don't believe this rally will last."
Gainers included telecoms company Telex -- one of the bourse's most volatile stocks -- which rose over four percent on foreign interest, said dealers.
They said they did not know any reason for the rise, but said the stock is very lightly traded so any demand automatically causes the price to jump.
Telex ended up 4.12 percent at 1,260 pesos.
Other winners included forestry firm Masisa, up 4.65 percent at 225 pesos and winery Concha y Toro, which rose 1.27 percent at 160 pesos.
Losers included steel-maker Cap, down 1.82 percent at 1,345 pesos, pulp producer Copec, down 1.51 percent at 1,832 pesos and power utility Enersis, which fell 0.95 percent to 259-1/2 pesos.
